name: templates-dir-validation
body: Templates dir validation: before any deck validation, render or serve (startup and every reload), kalide validates the resolved library root (the configured `templates:` path, else the local `templates/`; see external-template-library) — the loader's single resolution point — fail-fast in a fixed order: (1) `library.yaml` present and valid; (2) structure (templates-dir-layout: the library structure is library.yaml, slides/, sections/, themes/ and media/, and its template names are unique across slides/ and sections/. Every other top-level entry is ignored — the loader validates only the library itself, so a `.git/` directory, a README, a root-level `AGENTS.md` (library-guide-layout) or any other unrelated entry loads cleanly and stays inert: it is never parsed, validated, rendered, listed or served); (3) each template in kind-then-name order (slides/ then sections/): `template.yaml`, `layout.html.tmpl`, `example.md` present, `template.yaml` well-formed against the schema vocabulary (no `usage:` key), layout parses as standard html/template with the documented function set (template-language), parse errors file:line-qualified; (4) the template-build-checks across the set (requirements.constraint.template-registry-integrity); (5) each theme in name order has `theme.css`; (6) references resolve: in a theme's `theme.css` — and in every stylesheet it reaches through `@import`, wherever that stylesheet lives (the same theme directory, another theme, or `media/`) — each `@import` directive is followed in either form, the quoted-string form `@import "x.css";` and the `url()` form `@import url("x.css");`; an `@import` target with no reserved prefix resolves relative to the importing CSS file's own location, a `media:` target resolves under the resolved library's `media/` (the path after the prefix relative to `media/` and staying within it, like a layout `media "path"` argument), and a `theme:<name>/` target resolves under that theme's directory (an unknown `<name>` is a templates error); imports are followed bounded and cycle-safe, with a cycle detected across the whole import graph (including a theme↔media and a theme↔theme cycle); an `@import` target that is a missing file, an absolute path, a `..` escaping its tree, a reference outside the library, or any other scheme is a templates error naming the offending CSS file and line; in every served stylesheet each relative `url(…)` resolves to an existing file under the resolved library, a `url()` carrying the reserved `media:` prefix resolves to an existing file under the resolved library's `media/` (relative to `media/` and staying within it) exactly like a layout `media "path"` argument, and a `url()` carrying the reserved `theme:<name>/` prefix resolves to an existing file inside that theme's directory; every other scheme (http:, data:, //, …), an absolute path and a `..` escape are rejected with a templates error naming the offending CSS file and line; every relative src/href in layouts resolves to an existing file inside the resolved library; and every `media "path"` argument in a layout is a relative path inside `media/` naming an existing file under the resolved library's `media/` — a violation is a templates error qualified with the layout's file:line (requirements.constraint.media-paths-library-relative); (7) each example.md validates against its template and its layout executes (execute errors file:line-qualified). The first failure is reported as a templates error: path-qualified (e.g. `<library>/slides/content/template.yaml:12`), with a hint and closest-match suggestion where applicable, in the terminal at startup and in the full-page error on reload — the same error-reporting format as deck errors, labelled as a templates error. AC: one test per step shows the expected first error (step 6 includes a missing `media` file, a `..` argument and an absolute argument; a `media:` theme-CSS reference to a missing file and one with a `..` or absolute path; a `theme:<name>/` reference to an unknown theme and to a missing file; a `..`, absolute path or scheme in either prefixed form; an `@import` to a missing file, an absolute path or a `..` escape; and an `@import` cycle spanning a theme and `media/` or two themes; a clean `@import url('media:css/x.css')` and `@import url('theme:default/theme.css')` validate); a valid dir proceeds to deck validation.
